original_value: Sustainability is one of the main challenges of the recent decades. In this regard, several prior studies have used different techniques and approaches for solving this problem in the field of sustainability engineering. Multiple criteria decision making (MCDM) is an important technique that presents a systematic approach for helping decisionmakers in this field. The main goal of this paper is to review the literature concerning the application of MCDM methods in the field of sustainable engineering. The Web of Science (WoS) Core Collection Database was chosen to identify 108 papers in the period of 2008–2018. The selected papers were classified into five categories, including construction and infrastructure, supply chains, transport and logistics, energy, and other. In addition, the articles were classified based on author, year, application area, study objective and problem, applied methods, number of published papers, and name of the journal. The results of this paper show that sustainable engineering is an area that is quite suitable for the use of MCDM. It can be concluded that most of the methods used in sustainable engineering are based on traditional approaches with a noticeable trend towards applying the theory of uncertainty, such as fuzzy, grey, rough, and neutrosophic theory.

result.paraphrase: Sustainability has been among the major challenges of recent decades. In this context, previous studies have employed various techniques and approaches to address this issue within sustainability engineering. Multiple criteria decision making (MCDM) is a key method that offers a structured way to assist decisionmakers in this field. This paper aims to review the literature on the use of MCDM methods in sustainable engineering. Using the Web of Science (WoS) Core Collection Database, 108 papers published between 2008 and 2018 were identified. The selected papers were grouped into five categories: construction and infrastructure, supply chains, transport and logistics, energy, and other. The articles were also classified by author, year, application area, study objective and problem, applied methods, number of published papers, and journal name. The findings indicate that sustainable engineering is highly suitable for MCDM applications. It may be concluded that most methods used in sustainable engineering rely on traditional approaches, with a clear trend toward uncertainty-based theories such as fuzzy, grey, rough, and neutrosophic theory.
